text:
Minnesota has the best record in our tables at 18-4-6, and Kirill Kaprizov is playing like the reason. His point streak reached 15 games this week, a Wild record, and his line with Joel Eriksson Ek and Matt Boldy has outscored opponents 26-3 in 305 minutes at five on five. That is not a typo, and it is not sustainable at that ratio, but the line also takes 60% of the expected goals, so the dominance underneath is real.

The team is strong on process too: 55.8% of the expected goals, top of the West. The part to watch is the goaltending. Minnesota has allowed about 14 fewer goals than its shots deserve, which is the main reason our numbers have it about seven points ahead of what its chances earned. Jesper Wallstedt has carried most of the load (The Hockey News quotes him: "I Could Play More") and Filip Gustavsson's return, as The Athletic put it, makes the split "fluid."

Friday was the reminder of how thin margins are. The Wild led Colorado 3-0 late and lost in a shootout, with Quinn Hughes doubtful for the game. Hughes has 16 points in his last 10, and the pair of Hughes and Jared Spurgeon has 65% of the expected goals.

Our numbers give Minnesota a 99% chance at the playoffs and 55% at the division. What we'd watch: how John Hynes splits the net once Gustavsson is fully back, because the save percentage is doing more of the work than the standings let on.
